title: VESPER Claim
description: REM-010 §4.1. Grounding is tracked PER CLAIM, not per response. This is the artifact that makes 'no guessing' -- the most-repeated behavioural requirement in the corpus -- a mechanism rather than a disposition. Retrofitting per-claim evidence into a finished generation pipeline is a rewrite, not an addition, which is why it is a contract before any code exists. Authority: SR-041, SR-052; RB-001, RB-002, P-001; INV-EVID-1/2/3.

span.description: INV-EVID-2: every source_ref resolves to a REPRODUCIBLE retrieved span. A similarity score is never sufficient grounding -- this field is the difference between BAG and RAG, and its absence on a source_ref is what CI-033 fails.

support_type.description: `model_prior` means the model believes it without having retrieved, computed or observed it. It is a legitimate value -- the point is that it is SAYABLE, so the output gate can act on it.

policy_class.description: DF-OUTPUT-GATE input. The first four are the classes in which an unsupported assertion causes durable harm: it gets written down, acted on, or believed later.

trust_class.description: Inherited from the WEAKEST supporting fragment (REM-003 §4.4). A claim grounded in an external web page is retrieved_external no matter how confident the model is about it.

gate_disposition.description: DF-OUTPUT-GATE output, recorded on the claim so the decision is auditable after the fact rather than inferable from what was said.

unknown.description: INV-EVID-3. UNKNOWN is a first-class return value across BAG, world model and memory. An empty retrieval is never coerced into a plausible answer -- it produces a claim with unknown=true and no support, which the gate handles explicitly.

then.description: INV-EVID-1 as a schema property: in these four policy classes a model_prior claim CANNOT carry gate_disposition EMIT. The plain assertion is unexpressible, so an implementation cannot arrive at it innocently.
A claim that says it was retrieved must name what it retrieved.

$comment: EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: a response-level `grounded: true` flag. Response-level grounding is the natural implementation and it passes the 'mostly grounded with one unsupported specific' case that A-003 exists to fail.
